metadata.title: Frege: Sense, Reference, and Concept Script
Frege: Sense, Reference, and Concept Script

sections.text: Gottlob Frege (1848–1925) is the founder of modern logic and the direct ancestor of formal semantics, type theory, and the foundations of mathematics as the 20th century understood them. His work on sense and reference gave philosophy of language its central technical vocabulary. His concept notation (Begriffsschrift) gave us quantifiers and the predicate calculus. His project of reducing arithmetic to logic gave us the Frege-Russell tradition in foundations, and indirectly Russell's Paradox.

metadata.title: Frege: Sense, Reference, and Concept Script

sections.text: For a TCS background: Frege is the source of the predicate calculus you used in computability theory, the function/argument distinction underlying every λ-term, and the compositionality principle underlying every denotational semantics.
